data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise reporting what people said, including basic tense and pronoun changes.
learningPoints: Use said (that) + clause to report a statement.
Backshift present tenses when reporting from a past viewpoint.
Change pronouns and possessives when the speaker changes.
Change common time expressions where necessary.

sections.explain: Use SAID (THAT) + clause. SAID does not require a person object.

words.word: She said that she was tired.
She said me that she was tired.
She told that she was tired.
He told me that he was busy.
He told that he was busy.
He said me that he was busy.

sections.summary: Backshifting Present Simple to Past Simple.
sections.explain: A present tense often shifts back when reporting a past statement.

words.word: 'I work here.' → She said that she worked there.
'I work here.' → She said that she work there.
'I work here.' → She told that she worked there.

sections.explain: Present Continuous often becomes Past Continuous in reported speech.

words.word: 'I'm waiting.' → He said that he was waiting.
'I'm waiting.' → He said that he is wait.
'I'm waiting.' → He told that he was waiting.

sections.explain: Pronouns change according to who originally spoke and who is reporting.

words.word: Anna said, 'I like my job.' → Anna said that she liked her job.
Anna said, 'I like my job.' → Anna said that I liked my job.
Anna said, 'I like my job.' → Anna told that she liked her job.

sections.explain: WILL often changes to WOULD when reporting from a past viewpoint.

words.word: 'I'll call you.' → He said that he would call me.
'I'll call you.' → He said that he will called me.
'I'll call you.' → He told that he would call me.

sections.explain: CAN often becomes COULD in reported speech.

words.word: 'I can help.' → She said that she could help.
'I can help.' → She said that she can helped.
'I can help.' → She told that she could help.

sections.explain: NOW may change to THEN when the reporting time is later.

words.word: 'I'm busy now.' → He said that he was busy then.
'I'm busy now.' → He said that he is busy now yesterday.
'I'm busy now.' → He told that he was busy then.

sections.explain: TODAY may change to THAT DAY when the statement is reported later.

words.word: 'I'm working today.' → She said that she was working that day.
'I'm working today.' → She said that she worked today tomorrow.
'I'm working today.' → She told that she was working that day.

sections.explain: Keep the negative meaning while applying the reported-speech structure.

words.word: 'I don't know.' → He said that he didn't know.
'I don't know.' → He said that he doesn't knew.
'I don't know.' → He told that he didn't know.
